description: Renovate configuration for Proxmox infrastructure automation (Terraform, Docker Compose, Ansible)
dependencyDashboardHeader:
Tracks dependency updates for the Proxmox infrastructure automation (Terraform, Ansible, Komodo, service images).

**After merging**: apply the relevant Terraform/Ansible change or let Komodo redeploy the affected service; see the repo README for procedures.

---

Komodo Core image tag in the komodo_core role defaults
Komodo Periphery release in the komodo_periphery role defaults (stored without the v prefix; the installer URL adds it)
node_exporter release for the monitoring_agent role
Alloy release for the monitoring_agent role; keep it on the cluster DaemonSet's appVersion (argo-apps apps/infra/alloy)
cAdvisor release for the monitoring_agent role
FerretDB image for Komodo Core's database

postgres-documentdb image for Komodo Core's database. Compound tag <pg-major>-<documentdb>-ferretdb-<ferretdb>; the regex versioning pins the pg major as compatibility and compares the documentdb version plus the ferretdb major.minor. Comparable capture groups must be single numbers, so the ferretdb patch level is uncaptured — a tag differing ONLY in ferretdb patch won't be offered (documentdb bumps alongside every ferretdb release in practice)

Self-built unbound image tag in the pihole compose stack — looked up in Harbor, NOT upstream, so the compose bump is only offered once CI has pushed that tag. Tracking the NLnetLabs release here put the compose change in the same MR as the Dockerfile ARG, and Komodo redeployed on merge before build:unbound had pushed the image. semver versioning skips the latest and commit-SHA tags CI also pushes

Self-built pihole image tag (docker/pihole, pihole-updatelists baked in) in the pihole compose stacks — looked up in Harbor for the same reason as unbound: the compose bump is only offered once build:pihole has pushed the tag the Dockerfile FROM bump produced. semver versioning skips the latest and commit-SHA tags

Self-built semaphore image tag (docker/semaphore) in its compose stack, looked up in Harbor: the compose bump is only offered once build:semaphore has pushed the tag the Dockerfile ARG bump produced. semver versioning skips the latest and commit-SHA tags

pihole-updatelists commit in docker/pihole/Dockerfile. The project tags no releases, so track master by commit (git-refs). Merging rebuilds the pihole image under the same tag, and CI's komodo:redeploy-images rolls it out.

packageRules.description: Infrastructure updates - graduated stabilization soak by update type (patch 1d). Trusted vendor releases (Talos, Kubernetes, Terraform providers, Docker images, Ansible collections) still land quickly, but a short soak guards against same-day broken releases; CI catches breakage before merge. The .ci/docker/Dockerfile build base keeps its own 3/7/14-day delays from the shared preset. Critical OS/cluster deps (Talos, Kubernetes) keep their own rules below.
Infrastructure updates - minor soak.
Infrastructure updates - major soak.
Docker digest pinning - Pin floating tags to reproducible digests for infrastructure reliability
Docker Compose service images - Grouped by service directory
Custom Docker base images - Build validation
Debian base image for Unbound - Disable built-in dockerfile manager (handled by custom regex)
Debian base image for Unbound - Base OS updates
Unbound DNS resolver version - Core DNS service. Dockerfile ARGs only; merging this builds and pushes the image, and the pihole compose tag follows in its own MR (rule below)

Self-built unbound image in the pihole compose stack - one MR (overrides the per-service-dir group above). minimumReleaseAge:null: the upstream soak already ran on the Dockerfile MR, and Harbor returns no release timestamps, so the inherited services/** soak would hold this back indefinitely. pinDigests:false: the regex has no digest group, so a pin update finds nothing to replace
Self-built pihole image in the pihole compose stacks - both stacks in one MR. minimumReleaseAge:null and pinDigests:false for the same reasons as the unbound rule above
Self-built semaphore image in its compose stack. minimumReleaseAge:null and pinDigests:false for the same reasons as the unbound rule above
OpenSSL library version - Security library used by Unbound. Pinned to <4 until NLnet Labs ships an unbound release with OpenSSL 4.x support
dnscrypt-proxy version - Encrypted DNS proxy binary

Terraform unit versions.tf - Disabled because Terragrunt regenerates these from root.hcl on every init (root.hcl is the source of truth, tracked by the customManager above). The single-level glob deliberately excludes the hand-written modules/*/versions.tf, which Renovate DOES manage.

Terraform providers - Grouped updates for IaC validation. root.hcl is the source of truth for unit-level provider constraints (the unit versions.tf are regenerated from it); the hand-written modules/*/versions.tf carry their own constraints and are bumped in the same group so they stay aligned.
Ansible Galaxy collections - Configuration management

Komodo Core + Periphery - same release line, bumped together (control plane for every host's deploys). minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour:timestamp-optional is REQUIRED for Core: it comes from GHCR, whose registry API returns only {name, tags} with no release timestamps. Since Renovate 42 the default is timestamp-required, which treats a release with no timestamp as never having aged, so the ansible/** minimumReleaseAge soak held Core back indefinitely while Periphery (github-releases, which does carry timestamps) shipped alone every release. pinDigests:false: these are bare tags in ansible role defaults matched by [0-9.]+ regexes — a digest pin would rewrite them to tag@sha256 and the customManagers would stop matching (it also collides with the version bump inside the group branch). Do NOT set a versioning override: komodo-core publishes ~120 tags that are mostly SHA fragments and floating aliases (dev, latest, 2, 2.3) which docker versioning skips but semver cannot parse

FerretDB + postgres-documentdb for Komodo Core - the DocumentDB layer must match the FerretDB release, so they bump together. Both images are on GHCR, which returns no release timestamps, so timestamp-optional is needed here for the same reason as the komodo rule above — without it the ansible/** minimumReleaseAge soak holds both back indefinitely. pinDigests:false for the same reason as the komodo rule above
Talos OS version - Critical cluster OS updates

Kubernetes version - Capped at v1.35.x, matching the active Talos 1.13 cluster; the bound also keeps headroom for the Rancher 2.14 support matrix (1.33-1.35) should the Rancher/K3s path be brought back from .archive/.

PostgreSQL version pinning - bitwarden pinned to v16.x. The db (plain postgres) and backup (postgres-alpine) services share depName 'postgres'; they are kept on the SAME version (16.14) so Renovate doesn't hit a same-depName 'upgrade collision' (which neither grouping nor branch-splitting via matchCurrentValue resolved — it's a Renovate dedup limitation for two versions of one image in one file). Keeping them aligned is the reliable fix; this rule just holds the v16.x pin.
PostgreSQL version pinning - paperless-ngx pinned to v18.x
Redis version pinning - paperless-ngx pinned to v8.x
pihole-updatelists master commits. minimumReleaseAge:null: git-refs carries no release timestamps, so an inherited soak would hold every update forever (same reason as the Harbor image rules).
GitLab and its runner never automerge: they run the pipelines that gate every other automerge, so a broken patch there stops the whole loop. Overrides the preset's digest/pin/patch automerge.
